note: Hebrew neatsah means contempt or disgrace suffered by the people, not blasphemy uttered by them; the KJV word now suggests a different sin.

kjv: I (Yahweh) will send a blast upon him (Sennacherib)
mine: I (Yahweh) am about to put a spirit in him (Sennacherib)
note: Hebrew noten bo ruach means "put a spirit in him," i.e. an impulse or disposition that makes him withdraw on hearing a report; "blast" implies a destroying wind.
Hebrew kush is the Nubian kingdom on the upper Nile (modern Sudan) whose 25th-dynasty pharaoh Tirhakah ruled Egypt, not modern Ethiopia.
Hebrew yoshev hakkeruvim means "sitting (enthroned) on the cherubim," picturing the ark's cherubim as God's throne; "between" is supplied.
Hebrew yaar karmillo uses karmel as a common noun, "garden land, orchard," i.e. Lebanon's richest woodland, not Mount Carmel.

kjv: all the rivers of besieged places
note: Hebrew yeore matsor: yeor is the Nile word for streams/channels and matsor is a poetic name for Egypt (Mizraim), which the KJV read as matsor "siege."
Hebrew shaananekha means your complacency or arrogant ease; "tumult" follows an older guess from the parallel "rage."
Hebrew erets ararat names Urartu; the KJV follows the Septuagint/Vulgate's Armenia, a later name for the region.
